extraction_notes.note: The running-text descriptions of greedy subset selection (Sec. 2.1) and of iterative soft thresholding (Sec. 3.1) restate Algorithms 1 and 3; only the pseudocode environments are nodes (equation (6) inside the GSS prose is kept as its own node). Table 1, a summary of rates pointing to the theorems, is not extracted.

remark or claim+proof: the derivation of the soft-thresholding form (43) of the group lasso argues and concludes in one paragraph with no separately stated claim, so it is one remark containing equations (40)-(43).

Claims 1-3 in the proof of Theorem 1 are numbered and later cited, so they are Level-1 claims nested in their description-item steps; their arguments stay as proof steps (step rule 7), so they have no proves edges, only uses edges into the step that combines them.

Theorems 5 and 7 have no proof environment: the preceding prose justifications are proof nodes (confidence 0.7). Theorem 3 is only said to be proved as in Collier et al. (2017) and Proposition 5 is left to the reader; all four carry rigor semi_formal.

Proposition 2 is stated as a consequence of Theorem 1 of Collier et al. (2017) and marked external; Lemma 5 is a recalled well-known chi-squared bound (external, uncited), whereas Lemmas 6, 7 and 9 of the same section are proved here and marked paper.

Huber's contamination model is defined in the introduction and recalled in Section 3; only the introduction's fuller copy is a node. The symbol mu is introduced in the introduction (DP3) but operationally redefined by the robust model (24); the finishing step's warning about uses of mu without an edge from the introduction's definition was left, since those uses are covered by the robust-model definition.
